name: Ishbah
overview: Ishbah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as the son of Mered and Bithia according to 1 Chronicles 4:17. His lineage places him within the genealogical records of Judah, emphasizing his place among God's chosen people. There are no additional notes or details about his life beyond this familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Ishbah means 'he boasts, congratulates' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name recorded in Scripture. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries a meaning that may imply a character trait or familial hope.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ishbah as the son of Mered and Bithia, establishing his immediate family. Additionally, he is noted as the father of Eshtemoa, indicating his role as a progenitor within his lineage. These relationships are all referenced in 1 Chronicles 4:17-18.
scriptureSignificance: Ishbah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah, as documented in the chronicler's account. His mention alongside his parents and son highlights the continuity of God's covenant people through successive generations. Though not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion preserves the heritage through which the Messiah would eventually come, underscoring the faithfulness of God's promises.
